metadata.source: Oxford Handbook of Critical Care (4th Ed)
metadata.description: Critical ICU protocols for safety validation.

protocols.name: ACLS Cardiac Arrest
steps: Start CPR (30:2), give oxygen, attach monitor/defibrillator
Shockable: Shock, CPR 2min, Pulse check, Shock, CPR 2min + Adrenaline 1mg
Non-shockable: Adrenaline 1mg immediately, CPR 2min, check rhythm

protocols.name: Anaphylaxis
steps: Repeat IM Adrenaline every 5 mins if no improvement

protocols.name: Sepsis Bundle (1-Hour)
steps: Obtain blood cultures prior to antibiotics
Rapid administration of 30mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension/lactate ≥4
Apply vasopressors if hypotensive during/after fluid resuscitation (target MAP ≥65)

protocols.name: Acute Coronary Syndrome (STEMI)
steps: Assess for primary PCI (target door-to-balloon <90 mins)
If PCI >120 mins wait, consider fibrinolysis

protocols.name: Status Epilepticus
steps: IV Lorazepam 4mg (repeat once after 10-20 min if no effect)
If IV access unavailable: Buccal Midazolam 10mg or Rectal Diazepam 10mg
Second line: IV Phenytoin 15-20mg/kg or Levetiracetam 60mg/kg

protocols.name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
steps: Potassium replacement: Mandatory if K < 5.5 mmol/L
Target glucose fall 3 mmol/L/hr and ketone fall 0.5 mmol/L/hr

protocols.name: Severe Hyperkalemia
steps: Insulin-Glucose: 10 units Actrapid in 50mL 50% Dextrose over 15 min
Consider renal replacement therapy if refractory

protocols.name: Acute Asthma (Severe)
steps: Steroids: Prednisolone 40mg PO or Hydrocortisone 100mg IV
Consider IV Magnesium Sulfate 2g if life-threatening
Escalate to ICU if tiring or rising pCO2

protocols.name: Acute Pulmonary Edema
steps: GTN spray or IV infusion (if SBP >90)
Identify and treat underlying cause (AF, MI, HTN)

protocols.name: Acute Meningitis
steps: Immediate BC and LP (if no contraindications)
Dexamethasone 10mg IV Q6H (start with or before antibiotics)
